import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/training_4.csv"
]

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
# Use index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column as per Hint 24
dfs = [pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0) for path in source_files]

# All source tables have the exact same schema as the target:
# ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
# So we can safely concatenate (union) all source tables vertically.

# Concatenate all source DataFrames
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure columns are exactly in the target schema order
target_columns = ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

# Check and fix data types to match target schema (all strings)
# Convert all columns to string type explicitly
for col in target_columns:
    combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype(str)

# The target examples show that 'Winner' column values are "YES" or presumably "NO"
# We keep them as is, no transformation needed.

# Save the combined DataFrame to the target CSV path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
